data.label: Start Account Monitoring
data.description: Begin monitoring existing customer accounts for churn-risk signals in the CRM domain.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic workflow trigger/start event. It only initiates the process and does not require ML, NLP, or LLM reasoning. L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Collect Usage Signals
data.description: Gather product usage data and measure any drop over the last 30 days.
data.rationale: This step is a data retrieval and comparison task: fetch usage metrics and compute a 30-day drop. That is straightforward deterministic logic with simple aggregation and thresholding. No AI is needed, so L0 applies.

data.label: Check Support Sentiment
data.description: Identify support tickets tagged with negative sentiment for each account.
data.rationale: The step requires understanding or classifying ticket sentiment, which is an NLP/NLU task. L0 cannot interpret free-text support content, and this is narrower than generation. L2 is appropriate for sentiment detection/classification.

data.label: Check Payment Status
data.description: Detect late or failed invoice payments associated with each account.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic lookup and status check against billing records. It can be implemented with rules and database fields such as due date, paid status, and failure flags. No ML or language understanding is required, so L0 fits.

data.label: Score Churn Risk
data.description: Combine usage, support, and billing signals to assign a churn-risk score from 0 to 100.
data.rationale: The workflow asks for a numeric churn-risk score derived from multiple signals. While a rules-based score is possible at L0, the phrasing implies a predictive scoring function that could benefit from a trained model. L1 is justified because L0 cannot capture uncertainty/variation as well if the score is learned from historical churn outcomes. No language generation is needed.

data.label: Handle High Risk Account
data.description: Process accounts with churn-risk scores above 75 for immediate intervention.
data.rationale: This is a pure threshold-based decision gate: if score > 75, route to the high-risk path. It is fully deterministic and does not require AI. L0 is appropriate.

data.label: Notify CSM
data.description: Immediately notify the assigned Customer Success Manager about the high-risk account.
data.rationale: Notification delivery is a straightforward system action triggered by a rule. It does not involve interpretation or generation beyond templated messaging. L0 is sufficient.

data.label: Draft Retention Email
data.description: Create a personalized retention outreach email for the Customer Success Manager to use.
data.rationale: This step requires generating personalized natural-language content for outreach. That is a clear L3 use case: one LLM call to draft an email from account context and churn signals. No external tool use is inherently required for the drafting itself.

data.label: Handle Medium Risk Account
data.description: Process accounts with churn-risk scores between 40 and 75 for review planning.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic score-range check. The routing logic is purely rule-based and can be implemented with if/then/else conditions. L0 is enough.

data.label: Queue Weekly Review
data.description: Add the account to the weekly Customer Success Manager review queue.
data.rationale: Adding an account to a queue is a deterministic workflow action. It uses fixed criteria already resolved by the decision node and does not require AI. L0 applies.

data.label: Continue Passive Monitoring
data.description: Keep monitoring accounts with churn-risk scores below 40 without escalation.
data.rationale: This is a simple threshold-based branch for scores below 40. It is fully deterministic and does not need ML or language understanding. L0 is appropriate.

data.label: Log Scoring Decision
data.description: Record the churn-risk score and input signals used for audit purposes.
data.rationale: This is an audit logging operation that stores structured data: score and input signals. It is deterministic recordkeeping, not AI. L0 is sufficient.

message: This workflow is mostly deterministic orchestration (L0) for data collection, threshold routing, notifications, queueing, and audit logging. The main non-deterministic component is churn-risk scoring, which is best represented as L1 if learned from historical churn outcomes. The only language generation step is drafting a personalized retention email, which is L3. Overall, this is a low-to-moderate complexity automation with one NLP step for sentiment and one LLM drafting step.

workflow.workflowBrief: Monitor existing customer accounts for churn-risk signals: drop in product usage over the last 30 days, support tickets tagged negative-sentiment, and late or failed invoice payments. Score each account's churn risk from 0 to 100. For scores above 75, immediately notify the assigned Customer Success Manager and draft a personalized retention outreach email. For scores between 40 and 75, add the account to a weekly CSM review queue. For scores below 40, continue passive monitoring. Log every scoring decision with the input signals for audit.
